name: Documented ROCm failure modes: Vulkan PPL explosion, HIP gfx1151 corrupt output, HIP ubatch wrong logits
workarounds: llama.cpp issue #27506: ROCm backend PPL explosion (7.7 -> 3024) starting from b10040 - use b10038 or earlier
llama.cpp issue #27579: HIP/ROCm gfx1151 produces corrupted output while Vulkan is correct - use Vulkan backend for gfx1151
llama.cpp issue #28211: HIP/ROCm gfx1151 produces wrong logits for prompts longer than n_ubatch - keep n_ubatch >= prompt length
Always validate ROCm output against a known-good baseline (e.g., Vulkan or CPU) when upgrading ROCm versions
notes: Three documented ROCm failure modes in llama.cpp: (1) ISSUE #27506 - PPL EXPLOSION: ROCm backend severe perplexity explosion starting from build b10040. Bisect with concrete PPL values: b10038 = 7.7241, b10040 = 3024.3587, latest master = 2177.3497. Vulkan build unaffected. This demonstrates llama-perplexity as a corruption detector. (2) ISSUE #27579 - gfx1151 CORRUPT OUTPUT: HIP/ROCm backend produces corrupted output on gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S / Ryzen AI Max) while Vulkan is correct with byte-identical flags. Three-model matrix with two failure severities. The issue explicitly rules out the -f unsafe-math-optimizations removal as the cause. (3) ISSUE #28211 - HIP UBATCH WRONG LOGITS: HIP/ROCm on gfx1151 produces wrong logits (not a crash) for prompts longer than n_ubatch. Minimal public-API reproducer that decodes the same prompt twice differing only in n_ubatch. BF16 also affected (84.7476 vs 13.8167 on Vulkan), which rules out the quantized-matmul kernel as the cause. These failure modes are specific to gfx1151 (RDNA4 consumer silicon), not CDNA3/CDNA4 datacenter GPUs, but they illustrate the importance of validating ROCm output against known-good baselines.
